title: Landmark Supreme Court Cases
summary: A curated selection of landmark U.S. Supreme Court decisions with the question and holding.
source: U.S. Reports (Supreme Court opinions are U.S.-government public domain). Holdings summarized here in original wording. This is a curated selection, not the full docket.
template: {name} ({year}), {citation} — {topic}. Holding: {holding} (Some rulings have been limited or overruled by later cases.)

rows.name: Marbury v. Madison
rows.holding: Established judicial review — the Supreme Court can strike down laws that violate the Constitution.

rows.name: McCulloch v. Maryland
rows.topic: federal power / Necessary and Proper Clause
rows.holding: Congress has implied powers, and states cannot tax federal institutions; federal law is supreme.

rows.name: Gibbons v. Ogden
rows.holding: Federal power to regulate interstate commerce is broad and supersedes conflicting state law.

rows.name: Dred Scott v. Sandford
rows.holding: Held that enslaved people were not citizens — a ruling later nullified by the 13th and 14th Amendments. Widely condemned.

rows.name: Plessy v. Ferguson
rows.holding: Upheld 'separate but equal' racial segregation — overturned by Brown v. Board (1954).

rows.name: Schenck v. United States
rows.holding: Speech can be limited when it poses a 'clear and present danger' (later narrowed by Brandenburg).

rows.name: Gitlow v. New York
rows.holding: Began applying the Bill of Rights to the states through the 14th Amendment.

rows.name: Korematsu v. United States
rows.holding: Upheld Japanese-American internment — later repudiated as a grave error.

rows.name: Brown v. Board of Education
rows.holding: Racial segregation in public schools is unconstitutional; 'separate but equal' has no place in education.

rows.name: Mapp v. Ohio
rows.holding: Evidence obtained by illegal search cannot be used in state courts.

rows.name: Baker v. Carr
rows.holding: Courts may hear redistricting cases, leading to the 'one person, one vote' principle.

rows.name: Engel v. Vitale
rows.holding: Official school-sponsored prayer violates the First Amendment.

rows.name: Gideon v. Wainwright
rows.holding: States must provide an attorney to defendants who cannot afford one.

rows.name: Heart of Atlanta Motel v. United States
rows.holding: Congress can bar racial discrimination in public accommodations under the Commerce Clause.

rows.name: Miranda v. Arizona
rows.holding: Police must inform suspects of their rights (to remain silent, to an attorney) before interrogation.

rows.name: Loving v. Virginia
rows.holding: Laws banning interracial marriage are unconstitutional.

rows.name: Tinker v. Des Moines
rows.holding: Students don't 'shed their constitutional rights at the schoolhouse gate'; symbolic protest is protected.

rows.name: Brandenburg v. Ohio
rows.holding: Speech can be punished only if it incites 'imminent lawless action'.

rows.name: New York Times Co. v. United States
rows.holding: The government cannot use 'prior restraint' to block publication (the Pentagon Papers case).

rows.name: Furman v. Georgia
rows.holding: Struck down then-current death-penalty laws as arbitrary (cruel and unusual).

rows.name: Wisconsin v. Yoder
rows.holding: Amish families could not be compelled to send children to school past 8th grade.

rows.name: Roe v. Wade
rows.holding: Recognized a constitutional right to abortion — overruled by Dobbs (2022).

rows.name: United States v. Nixon
rows.holding: Executive privilege is not absolute; the President had to turn over the Watergate tapes.

rows.name: Gregg v. Georgia
rows.holding: The death penalty is constitutional under properly structured sentencing laws.

rows.name: Regents of the Univ. of California v. Bakke
rows.holding: Racial quotas in admissions are unconstitutional, but race may be one factor (later limited).

rows.name: New Jersey v. T.L.O.
rows.holding: Schools may search students on 'reasonable suspicion,' a lower bar than probable cause.

rows.name: Texas v. Johnson
rows.holding: Flag burning is protected symbolic political speech.

rows.name: Bush v. Gore
rows.holding: Halted the Florida recount, effectively deciding the 2000 presidential election.

rows.name: District of Columbia v. Heller
rows.holding: The Second Amendment protects an individual right to keep a handgun for self-defense at home.

rows.name: Citizens United v. FEC
rows.holding: The government cannot limit independent political spending by corporations and unions.

rows.name: Obergefell v. Hodges
rows.holding: Same-sex couples have a constitutional right to marry nationwide.

rows.name: Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization
rows.holding: Overruled Roe v. Wade, returning abortion regulation to the states.
